assessment.nobel_worthiness: A consequential, coherent political-economy programme linking political institutions, state capacity, fiscal choices and development.
assessment.attribution: Besley, Persson and Tabellini are central and complementary contributors to the listed body of theory and empirical political economy.
assessment.maturity: The agenda has shaped research for decades and is highly relevant to enduring questions of governance and prosperity.
uncertainties: The broad programme has many important contributors, making the boundary of a three-person award contestable.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Law and finance recast the study of investor protection and financial development and generated a major comparative research agenda.
assessment.attribution: La Porta, Lopez-de-Silanes and Shleifer are core authors of the foundational legal-origins work.
assessment.maturity: Its influence and extensive subsequent testing make this a mature contribution.
uncertainties: The strength and causal interpretation of legal-origins claims remain debated.
Robert W. Vishny is also a central credited contributor.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: This work transformed understanding of how technology and trade reshape tasks, local labour markets and inequality.
assessment.attribution: Autor, Dorn and Hanson form a clear core for the influential empirical evidence on these mechanisms.
assessment.maturity: The findings have accumulated over a long period and remain central to economic and policy debate.
uncertainties: Separating trade effects from technological change and other local shocks is empirically demanding.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The reconstruction of top-income and wealth distributions has profoundly changed research and public understanding of long-run inequality.
assessment.attribution: Piketty, Saez and Zucman are leading architects of the linked measurement and analysis programme.
assessment.maturity: The data infrastructure and resulting literature are extensive and have endured substantial scholarly scrutiny.
uncertainties: Measurement of wealth, tax avoidance and offshore assets entails difficult assumptions and incomplete observability.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Partial identification supplied a fundamental framework for drawing credible conclusions when point identification is unwarranted.
assessment.attribution: Manski is the seminal figure in establishing the core conceptual approach.
assessment.maturity: The framework is long established and broadly used across econometrics and applied research.
uncertainties: Allocating credit between the foundational framework and its later extensions requires care.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Dynamic-panel GMM methods made a lasting methodological contribution to empirical work with longitudinal data.
assessment.attribution: Arellano, Blundell and Bond are closely identified with the central estimators and their development.
assessment.maturity: The methods are mature, foundational and widely applied.
uncertainties: Widespread application has also revealed sensitivity to instrument proliferation and specification choices.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Their work supplied powerful economic tools for thinking about exhaustible resources, natural capital and sustainability.
assessment.attribution: Dasgupta and Heal are clear foundational contributors to the listed research programme.
assessment.maturity: The work is long-standing and increasingly salient as biodiversity and inclusive-wealth measurement enter policy debate.
uncertainties: Valuing ecological assets and aggregating them into inclusive wealth remain methodologically and ethically contested.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Audit and correspondence studies provided vivid, influential evidence on discrimination and improved the empirical study of unequal treatment.
assessment.attribution: Bertrand and Mullainathan are leading credited contributors to the modern experimental approach.
assessment.maturity: The design has been replicated extensively and has had durable methodological and policy impact.
uncertainties: Audit-study estimates concern particular stages and settings and do not by themselves identify all mechanisms or aggregate labour-market effects.
Kerwin Kofi Charles is also a significant credited contributor.
